course_description: The course is about understanding what it means to be a user of a computer and, therefore, how to create related products and services that work seamlessly. This course provides a comprehensive introduction and deep dive into HCI, so students can create designs that provide outstanding user experiences. This course provides a deep understanding of what it means to be a user and how to implement user-centered design for the best possible results.

course_learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts about the relevance of human and computer interaction, including their abilities and limitations.

topic_learning_outcomes.text: Describe what interaction design and how it relates to human –computer interaction and other fields.
Discuss the use of interface metaphors and interaction types as part of a conceptual model.
Show the difference between classic internal cognitive frameworks and more recent external cognitive approaches that have been applied in HCI.

course_learning_outcomes.text: Use different techniques and concepts of the human computer interaction in creating interface design for computer/IT applications.
Apply a variety of simple methods for evaluating the quality of a user interface.
Evaluate the methods and techniques used in design for usability requirements.

topic_learning_outcomes.text: Discuss how to plan and run a successful data gathering program.
Explain some advantages of involving users in development.
Analyze data gathered from questionnaires, interviews and observations.
Understand the essential characteristics of good design
Describe prototyping and different types of prototyping activities.
Explain how to do usability testing. TLO15. Explain how do heuristic evaluation and walkthroughs.
